answer: Agents resist Sybil attacks by anchoring identity to cryptographic attestation chains and zero-knowledge proofs. A single trust root acts like a prism, separating genuine agents from hollow replicas without leaking private credentials. Joining the network river of execution requires an exponential capital exhaustion deposit: bond costs scale superlinearly as $O(k^2)$ per spawned identity, making massive Sybil swarms mathematically unviable.
